notes: Version 2.70 records ENI 2.11's gauge statements. Definition 3 fixes a minimal sense of gauge structure arising from the projection: an effective, fibre-preserving action of a group by automorphisms of the configuration space, that is, a subgroup of the group of projection-preserving automorphisms. Proposition 4 (proved, elementary and independent of Theorem 3) shows that an injective projection admits only the trivial such structure, so a non-trivial one requires non-injectivity. In that minimal sense the converse holds for a non-injective projection exactly when the group of projection-preserving automorphisms is non-trivial: always for a non-injective projection between bare sets, not in general when automorphisms must preserve further structure. No gauge structure in the physical sense is derived: a non-trivial Lie structure group, a supplied principal bundle of which the projection is either the bundle itself or a bundle associated with it, a representation, a connection and its dynamics are supplied hypotheses, and the structure group is not the group of projection-preserving automorphisms (Remark 4). The dependency edges are unchanged; only the ENI node description of the graph changes.
